data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This regulation describes the processing, management, and response policy for all correspondence received by the Department.
policy_statements.target: all correspondence received by the Department

policy_statements.source_text: Departmental Regulation 3060-1, USDA Correspondence Management Regulation, dated January 26, 1989, is hereby superseded.
cross_references: Departmental Regulation 3060-1, USDA Correspondence Management Regulation, dated January 26, 1989

policy_statements.source_text: Correspondence shall be used to communicate within and outside the Department.
It will not be used to establish, change, or rescind policies, procedures, or instructions contained in Departmental or agency directives.
policy_statements.target: policies, procedures, or instructions contained in Departmental or agency directives

policy_statements.source_text: All correspondence shall use clear, accessible, and concise language and style.
It shall be written in a manner appropriate for the correspondent, accounting for level of expertise, educational background, and any physical limitations to the extent possible.
conditions: to the extent possible

policy_statements.source_text: Received correspondence shall be responded to in a timely and appropriate manner.
It shall answer the concerns and inquiries of the correspondent to the maximum extent possible.
conditions: to the maximum extent possible
policy_statements.target: concerns and inquiries of the correspondent

policy_statements.source_text: Each agency and staff office shall establish and maintain a correspondence management system in accordance with this directive.
conditions: in accordance with this directive

policy_statements.source_text: All Priority Correspondence shall be recorded in a single Departmental system.
Other sources which provide general guidance on correspondence management, style preferences, information security, etc., are:
DR 0100-1, Departmental Directives System;
DR3080-001, Records Management;
DR3090-001, Litigation Retention Policy for Documentary Materials including Electronically Stored Information;
cross_references: DR3090-001, Litigation Retention Policy for Documentary Materials including Electronically Stored Information

DR3440-002, Control and Protection of Sensitive Security Information;

cross_references: DR5160-001, Official Seal of the Department

cross_references: USDA Stationery Systems, Office of Communications (OC), USDA

cross_references: U.S. Government Correspondence Manual, Government Accountability Office (GAO)

policy_statements.source_text: U.S. Government Style Manual, Government Printing Office (GPO)
cross_references: U.S. Government Style Manual, Government Printing Office (GPO)

policy_statements.source_text: Agency refers to a bureau, mission area, and departmental staff office, as defined in DR1010-001, Organization.
Campaign Correspondence is a subset of correspondence.
Campaign correspondence refers to mass produced or organizationally instigated correspondence.
Such correspondence is usually electronic (email or fax), often generated from a Web site, and typically advocates for a specific policy or action by the Department.
This class of correspondence does not include public comments made in response to a proposed regulatory action.
Clearance is the formal act of approving the content within a document.
It also refers to the business process for ensuring the review and approval of documents.
Clearing Official refers to an official who has been requested to clear draft correspondence by a Signing Official.
Controlled Correspondence is correspondence that is formally received, tracked, and managed using a correspondence management system.
Correspondence refers to official written communications.
Correspondence may be internal or external in nature, and may be transmitted in person or through mail, fax, or email.
Immediate Office of the Secretary refers to the office containing the Secretary, Deputy Secretary, and their immediate staff.

Office of the Secretary refers to the office containing the Immediate Office of the Secretary, the offices of all Under and Assistant Secretaries, and Departmental Staff Offices which report directly to the Secretary.
Priority Correspondence is a subset of correspondence.
All Priority Correspondence shall be controlled correspondence.
It includes:

All correspondence received from elected or appointed Federal, State, local, foreign, and Tribal officials, members of Congress, and Governors that is received by the Office of the Secretary and senior agency officials.

At the discretion of the addressee it may also be expanded to include other categories of important correspondence, such as correspondence received from major trade associations, academic institutions, or international organizations.
conditions: At the discretion of the addressee

policy_statements.source_text: Protected Information refers to all information designated as classified, sensitive, or personally identifiable.
Distribution and disclosure of protected information within correspondence is subject to additional regulations.
For additional information see:
Appendix A;
DR3440-001, Safeguarding Classified Information;
DR3440-002, Control and Protection of Sensitive Security Information;
cross_references: DR3440-002, Control and Protection of Sensitive Security Information

policy_statements.source_text: DR3550-02, Sensitive But Unclassified (SBU) Information Protection;
cross_references: DR3550-02, Sensitive But Unclassified (SBU) Information Protection

policy_statements.source_text: Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. 552); and,
Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552).
Secretarial Correspondence is correspondence addressed to the Secretary and Deputy Secretary.
All Secretarial Correspondence is controlled correspondence.
Signing Official refers to the official who is designated to sign an individual piece of correspondence.
Under Secretaries, Assistant Secretaries, Agency Heads, and Staff Office Directors shall:

Designate a Controlled Correspondence Officer and a Correspondence Liaison to serve as direct contact points with the Office of the Executive Secretariat (OES) for Priority Secretarial Correspondence; and,
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Assistant Secretaries, Agency Heads, and Staff Office Directors
policy_statements.target: Controlled Correspondence Officer and a Correspondence Liaison

policy_statements.source_text: Ensure agency personnel comply with deadlines for the preparation of responses to received correspondence, as established by the Secretary.
policy_statements.actor_name: Under Secretaries, Assistant Secretaries, Agency Heads, and Staff Office Directors

policy_statements.source_text: The Agency Controlled Correspondence Officer (CCO) shall:
Report to the Director of Public Affairs, or an equivalent position within the organization, on matters related to Secretarial Correspondence;
policy_statements.target: Director of Public Affairs, or an equivalent position within the organization

policy_statements.source_text: Internally track all controlled correspondence and ensure that a response to this correspondence is provided within ten working days of receipt by the agency; and,
conditions: within ten working days of receipt by the agency

policy_statements.source_text: Serve as the primary point of contact to OES for all matters related to Secretarial Correspondence.
The Correspondence Liaison shall:
Report to the Under Secretary, Assistant Secretary, Agency Head, or Staff Office Director on matters related to Secretarial Correspondence;
policy_statements.target: Under Secretary, Assistant Secretary, Agency Head, or Staff Office Director

policy_statements.source_text: Periodically review the quality and timeliness of all controlled correspondence managed or prepared by the agency;
policy_statements.target: quality and timeliness of all controlled correspondence managed or prepared by the agency

policy_statements.source_text: Lead internal efforts to improve the agency’s correspondence program.
policy_statements.target: internal efforts to improve the agency’s correspondence program

policy_statements.source_text: Departmental Agencies and Staff Offices shall:
Consistent with Departmental standards, develop policies, standards, and procedures for internal correspondence management;
policy_statements.target: policies, standards, and procedures for internal correspondence management
conditions: Consistent with Departmental standards

policy_statements.source_text: Establish management controls to ensure appropriate levels of quality and timeliness, including the management and preparation of correspondence;
Ensure all Priority Correspondence is entered into the Departmental correspondence management system;
Provide their staff with training in correspondence practices; and,
Prepare and review all Secretarial Correspondence in a timely manner, including special requests from the Immediate Office of the Secretary as requested by OES.
conditions: as requested by OES

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of the Executive Secretariat (OES) shall:
Serve as liaison between the Immediate Office of the Secretary and agencies regarding Secretarial Correspondence matters;
policy_statements.target: Immediate Office of the Secretary and agencies

policy_statements.source_text: Manage the clearance process of Secretarial Correspondence and determine whether changes or redrafting is necessary;
Review draft Secretarial Correspondence for grammatical errors, format, and consistency in the letters;
Process and dispatch signed Secretarial Correspondence;
Maintain a single Departmental correspondence management system and related IT systems for controlling Secretarial and Priority Correspondence;
policy_statements.target: single Departmental correspondence management system and related IT systems

policy_statements.source_text: Provide data to the Secretary and senior officials on agency performance with regards to assigned Secretarial correspondence activities on a regular basis and as requested;
conditions: on a regular basis and as requested

policy_statements.source_text: Maintain and publish an updated list of all Agency Correspondence Liaisons and Correspondence Control Officers;
policy_statements.target: updated list of all Agency Correspondence Liaisons and Correspondence Control Officers

policy_statements.source_text: Develop general policies, standards, reports, and procedures necessary for maintaining an effective and efficient correspondence management program;
policy_statements.target: general policies, standards, reports, and procedures

policy_statements.source_text: Provide general assistance and advice on matters related to correspondence, as requested by agencies; and,
conditions: as requested by agencies

policy_statements.source_text: Review agency correspondence management programs and practices to evaluate compliance with the provisions of this regulation.
policy_statements.target: agency correspondence management programs and practices

policy_statements.source_text: The Foreign Agricultural Service (FAS) shall:

Serve as the official liaison for correspondence between USDA agencies and the Department of State and its missions abroad, the U.S. Agency for International Development, and the U.S. Trade Representative.
policy_statements.target: USDA agencies and the Department of State and its missions abroad, the U.S. Agency for International Development, and the U.S. Trade Representative

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of the General Counsel (OGC) shall:
Review all correspondence and associated reports and documents pertaining to outstanding litigation by or against the Department, or which raise particular legal questions;
policy_statements.target: all correspondence and associated reports and documents pertaining to outstanding litigation by or against the Department, or which raise particular legal questions
conditions: pertaining to outstanding litigation by or against the Department, or which raise particular legal questions

policy_statements.source_text: Review all correspondence to the Comptroller General; and,
policy_statements.target: all correspondence to the Comptroller General

policy_statements.source_text: Review other priority correspondence upon the request of the Secretary.
conditions: upon the request of the Secretary

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA), Office of the Chief Financial Officer shall:
Serve as official liaison between the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and USDA agencies;
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA), Office of the Chief Financial Officer
policy_statements.target: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) and USDA agencies

policy_statements.source_text: Review all correspondence between Members of Congress and USDA regarding proposed legislation;
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA), Office of the Chief Financial Officer
policy_statements.target: all correspondence between Members of Congress and USDA regarding proposed legislation

policy_statements.source_text: Review all correspondence concerning the proposed and enacted budget of USDA and its agencies, and associated budgetary and resource management issues;
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA), Office of the Chief Financial Officer
policy_statements.target: all correspondence concerning the proposed and enacted budget of USDA and its agencies, and associated budgetary and resource management issues

policy_statements.source_text: Review all correspondence concerning proposed regulatory and legislative issues; and,
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA), Office of the Chief Financial Officer
policy_statements.target: all correspondence concerning proposed regulatory and legislative issues

policy_statements.source_text: Review other priority correspondence upon the request of the Secretary.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of Budget and Program Analysis (OBPA), Office of the Chief Financial Officer
conditions: upon the request of the Secretary

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Inspector General (OIG) shall:
Serve as official liaison for correspondence between the Government Accountability Office (GAO) and USDA agencies;
policy_statements.target: Government Accountability Office (GAO) and USDA agencies

policy_statements.source_text: Review all correspondence to the Comptroller General regarding audits and investigations;
policy_statements.target: all correspondence to the Comptroller General regarding audits and investigations

policy_statements.source_text: Review all correspondence concerning OIG investigations and audits; and,
policy_statements.target: all correspondence concerning OIG investigations and audits

policy_statements.source_text: Review all correspondence concerning ongoing and completed investigations of employee misconduct.
policy_statements.target: all correspondence concerning ongoing and completed investigations of employee misconduct

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Congressional Relations (OCR) shall:
Review all Secretarial Correspondence to Members of Congress, Governors, and State, county, and local officials.

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of Tribal Relations (OTR) shall:
Review all Secretarial Correspondence to Tribal officials.
policy_statements.target: all Secretarial Correspondence to Tribal officials

policy_statements.source_text: All correspondence addressed to the Secretary is controlled correspondence unless otherwise determined by the Director of OES.
conditions: unless otherwise determined by the Director of OES

policy_statements.source_text: All priority correspondence shall also be controlled correspondence.
Other officers and officials of USDA may determine which of their correspondence is to be considered controlled correspondence.
policy_statements.actor_name: Other officers and officials of USDA
policy_statements.target: which of their correspondence is to be considered controlled correspondence

policy_statements.source_text: All statements of current or planned policy will be signed by the Secretary or the appropriate Under Secretary, Assistant Secretary, or Agency Head.
policy_statements.actor_name: Secretary or the appropriate Under Secretary, Assistant Secretary, or Agency Head
policy_statements.target: All statements of current or planned policy

policy_statements.source_text: Unless otherwise designated in this directive or agency policy, the addressee of received correspondence shall be the Signing Official.
conditions: Unless otherwise designated in this directive or agency policy

policy_statements.source_text: That official shall reserve the right to delegate the signature authority to appropriate employees.
All relevant policy should be clearly understood prior to the delegation of signature authority.
conditions: prior to the delegation of signature authority

policy_statements.source_text: Clearance refers to the official process of submitting a draft document for review and approval by a USDA official.
With regards to correspondence, clearance may include ensuring factual accuracy, proper grammar and formatting, legal sufficiency, and alignment with relevant existing policy and priorities.
In addition to the roles and responsibilities established in this Directive, the Signing Official shall have sole discretion to establish the clearance process for all correspondence they sign.
policy_statements.target: clearance process for all correspondence they sign
conditions: for all correspondence they sign

policy_statements.source_text: The process may include the names or titles of Clearing Officials, the type of clearance (e.g. policy, legal, grammatical), and the timeframe for completing the clearance.
As a courtesy, Clearing Officials will be afforded no less than two working days to review all non-Priority correspondence.
Clearing Officials shall identify all clearances as approved, not approved, or approved only with proposed changes.
They may also document and return any edits, comments, or additional information to the Signing Official as part of their clearance.
policy_statements.target: any edits, comments, or additional information
conditions: as part of their clearance

policy_statements.source_text: All correspondence shall conform to the grammatical and stylistic guidelines set forth in referenced directives, specifications, and style guides.
Questions may be addressed to OES.
All correspondence shall be managed and preserved in accordance with the Federal Records Act, Departmental and Agency regulations, applicable record schedules, and all other applicable guidance.

Secretarial correspondence, and all associated records generated during the analysis, drafting, and clearance of responses, are part of the Official Records of the Office of the Secretary, and shall be stored, handled, and preserved in accordance with guidance provided by OES.
policy_statements.target: Secretarial correspondence, and all associated records generated during the analysis, drafting, and clearance of responses

policy_statements.source_text: The guidance provided in this paragraph must be implemented consistently with the Freedom of Information Act and the Privacy Act and their implementing regulations, Subparts A and G, Part 1 of Title 7, Code of Federal Regulations.
cross_references: Subparts A and G, Part 1 of Title 7, Code of Federal Regulations

policy_statements.source_text: In addition, matters of policy and information of a policy nature shall be made public only by officials with appropriate authority.
policy_statements.target: matters of policy and information of a policy nature

policy_statements.source_text: The following restrictions apply to the disclosure of information within correspondence:
Secretarial Correspondence.
Correspondence prepared for the Secretary's signature may not be made public before it is signed and has been released through appropriate channels.
policy_statements.target: Correspondence prepared for the Secretary's signature
conditions: before it is signed and has been released through appropriate channels

policy_statements.source_text: White House Correspondence.
Correspondence referred from the White House to this Department shall not be made public in whole or in part, nor shall employees quote from any of these letters, unless required by law.

This regulation describes the processing, management, and response policy for all correspondence received by the Department.

Departmental Regulation 3060-1, USDA Correspondence Management Regulation, dated January 26, 1989, is hereby superseded.
Departmental Regulation 3060-1, USDA Correspondence Management Regulation, dated January 26, 1989
Correspondence shall be used to communicate within and outside the Department.
It will not be used to establish, change, or rescind policies, procedures, or instructions contained in Departmental or agency directives.
policies, procedures, or instructions contained in Departmental or agency directives
All correspondence shall use clear, accessible, and concise language and style.
It shall be written in a manner appropriate for the correspondent, accounting for level of expertise, educational background, and any physical limitations to the extent possible.
Received correspondence shall be responded to in a timely and appropriate manner.
It shall answer the concerns and inquiries of the correspondent to the maximum extent possible.
concerns and inquiries of the correspondent
Each agency and staff office shall establish and maintain a correspondence management system in accordance with this directive.
All Priority Correspondence shall be recorded in a single Departmental system.

Agency  refers to a bureau, mission area, and departmental staff office, as defined in DR1010-001, Organization.
Campaign Correspondence  is a subset of correspondence.
Campaign correspondence refers to mass produced or organizationally instigated correspondence.
Such correspondence is usually electronic (email or fax), often generated from a Web site, and typically advocates for a specific policy or action by the Department.
This class of correspondence does not include public comments made in response to a proposed regulatory action.
Clearance  is the formal act of approving the content within a document.
It also refers to the business process for ensuring the review and approval of documents.
Clearing Official  refers to an official who has been requested to clear draft correspondence by a Signing Official.
Controlled Correspondence  is correspondence that is formally received, tracked, and managed using a correspondence management system.
Correspondence  refers to official written communications.
Correspondence may be internal or external in nature, and may be transmitted in person or through mail, fax, or email.
Immediate Office of the Secretary  refers to the office containing the Secretary, Deputy Secretary, and their immediate staff.

Office of the Secretary  refers to the office containing the Immediate Office of the Secretary, the offices of all Under and Assistant Secretaries, and Departmental Staff Offices which report directly to the Secretary.
Priority Correspondence  is a subset of correspondence.
All Priority Correspondence shall be controlled correspondence.

All correspondence received from elected or appointed Federal, State, local, foreign, and Tribal officials, members of Congress, and Governors that is received by the Office of the Secretary and senior agency officials.

At the discretion of the addressee it may also be expanded to include other categories of important correspondence, such as correspondence received from major trade associations, academic institutions, or international organizations.
At the discretion of the addressee
Protected Information  refers to all information designated as classified, sensitive, or personally identifiable.
Distribution and disclosure of protected information within correspondence is subject to additional regulations.

Clearance refers to the official process of submitting a draft document for review and approval by a USDA official.
With regards to correspondence, clearance may include ensuring factual accuracy, proper grammar and formatting, legal sufficiency, and alignment with relevant existing policy and priorities.
In addition to the roles and responsibilities established in this Directive, the Signing Official shall have sole discretion to establish the clearance process for all correspondence they sign.
clearance process for all correspondence they sign
The process may include the names or titles of Clearing Officials, the type of clearance (e.g. policy, legal, grammatical), and the timeframe for completing the clearance.
As a courtesy, Clearing Officials will be afforded no less than two working days to review all non-Priority correspondence.
Clearing Officials shall identify all clearances as approved, not approved, or approved only with proposed changes.
They may also document and return any edits, comments, or additional information to the Signing Official as part of their clearance.
